title: How Sam Bankman-Fried Actually Lost $8 Billion
hook: He ran a crypto exchange worth $32 billion and gave himself a secret backdoor into every customer's account -- then $8 billion of it vanished in ten days.
body:
Sam Bankman-Fried left a Jane Street trading desk in 2017 to found Alameda Research, then co-founded the crypto exchange FTX in 2019 with Gary Wang. By January 2022 FTX was valued at $32 billion, and Bankman-Fried -- rumpled T-shirt, cargo shorts, a Super Bowl ad, tens of millions in political donations -- was crowned crypto's most trusted face. Underneath it, Alameda Research ran on a secret code exception that let it draw an uncapped, unmonitored line against customer deposits, propped up by FTX's own token, FTT. When CoinDesk published Alameda's balance sheet on November 2, 2022, and Binance's CZ announced he'd dump FTX's own token six days later, a ten-day bank run emptied the company: withdrawals froze, the Binance rescue collapsed, and FTX filed for bankruptcy on November 11, 2022. Bankman-Fried was arrested in the Bahamas the night before he was due to testify to Congress, convicted on all seven counts of fraud and conspiracy on November 2, 2023, and sentenced to 25 years in federal prison on March 28, 2024, with an $11 billion forfeiture order. This is what the SEC and DOJ complaints, the trial record, and the sentencing record actually say happened.
